statement: At 1024 B / 112 px the modern codecs keep verification EER within a few hundredths of a percent of the uncompressed reference.
JPEG-AI leads on identity cosine at the 224 px / 1024 B headline cell; Ours-ACCURATE is the runner-up, ahead of AVIF and WebP; legacy JPEG collapses.
metric: id-cos jpeg_ai / ours_accurate / avif / webp / jpeg

statement: Halving the budget to 512 B collapses the block codecs while the byte-budgeted learned codecs degrade gracefully.
Classical codecs are flat at >=960 B but spike below ~800 B, while byte-budgeted Ours-ACCURATE stays flat across the whole range (H4).
metric: AVIF EER at 512/768/960/1024 B vs Ours-ACCURATE

statement: PSNR does not reliably predict verification EER across codecs at matched budget: the rank correlation is non-significant at 1024 B and only moderate at 512 B.
metric: Spearman rho (PSNR vs EER), 1024 B / 512 B

statement: Ours-ACCURATE trails ~6 dB in PSNR yet posts the best LPIPS/DISTS of the field, consistent with its perceptual training objective.
The codec ranking is backbone-invariant: the matcher roster ranks the codecs almost identically (strong concordance).

On the held-out CVLFace-IR101 matcher (independent of the EdgeFace side-stream), Ours-ACCURATE is the best codec on KK at both budgets and on ColorFERET at 512 B; JPEG-AI leads it only at ColorFERET 1024 B.
The binary-search encoder uses nearly the whole byte budget: the median byte fill for Ours-ACCURATE is ~0.98 of the target.

Compression widens the Monk skin-tone EER disparity relative to the uncompressed baseline; JPEG 2000 amplifies it by roughly an order of magnitude while the strong codecs stay within ~2x (uniform MST5/6/7/9/10 basis).
The learned codec sits inside the strong-codec disparity band on the same uniform basis (no added skin-tone disparity at 1024 B).
metric: Ours-ACCURATE vs WebP vs JPEG2000 disparity (arcface)

statement: The worst 1024 B recompression chain on both datasets is JPEG XL re-encoded as HEIF; every chain through JPEG 2000 stays poor, while same-codec and modern-to-modern chains are benign (<~1 pp delta).
At 512 B a new catastrophic chain appears: JPEG 2000 re-encoded as JPEG leaves verification barely above chance.
The byte budget dominates sanitization: at eps=0.06 the residual identity gap under JPEG shrinks about fivefold from 1024 B to 512 B; JPEG 2000 is the strongest sanitizer at every grid point.
metric: JPEG residual 1024/512 B; JPEG2000 residual 1024 B (eps=0.06, CF)

statement: The trained codecs sanitize like the weaker classical codecs, not like JPEG 2000, and the higher-quality variant is the weaker defense (the refine head re-injects fine detail).
metric: KK residual eps=0.06/512B ours_accurate / ours_fast / jpeg2000

statement: After BH correction only two modern-codec pairs are statistically indistinguishable on ColorFERET; on KK the larger trial count resolves all codec-vs-codec pairs as significant (the single non-significant row is the Ours-ACCURATE vs Ours-FAST head-to-head under LVFace-L at 224 px), though the modern-codec AUC gaps remain operationally negligible.
metric: CF non-significant pairs; KK non-significant of total

statement: Classical encode cost spans three orders of magnitude (JPEG to HEIF); the learned codecs are near-symmetric and recover most of their CPU cost on GPU.
metric: encode ms: jpeg / heif (CPU); ours_accurate CPU->GPU

statement: Downsampling 224 -> 112 px retains virtually all spectral energy and (for strong matchers) embedding cosine, making 112 px the operating sweet spot under a fixed byte budget.
metric: AC energy retained at 112 px vs 224
